subject: social
title: Solve It Together
about: Working out everyday disagreements: fairness, asking for a turn, listening to both sides, calming down, compromise, making it right after sorry, when to get a grown-up, and how a class decides together by raising hands and voting. NC 1.B.1.4 (how disagreements are settled), 1.C&G.1.2 (how groups make rules and choices) and 1.C&G.1.3 (responsibilities of citizens).
tip: Next time two kids want the same thing, ask him: what are two fair ways to solve it?

cards.q: Ten kids and ten cookies. Each kid gets one cookie. Is that fair or unfair?
cards.note: Fair means everyone is treated the same way.

cards.q: Max swings all of recess. Zoe waits and waits for a turn. Is that fair or unfair?
cards.note: A fair recess means Zoe gets to swing too.

cards.q: Leo wants the truck Mia is playing with. What can Leo do?
cards.note: Asking nicely works better than grabbing. Then wait for your turn.

cards.q: Two kids want the same blocks. They build one big tower together. What is that called?
Two kids both want the swing. How can they know when it is time to switch?
cards.note: A timer or counting to twenty makes turns fair.

cards.q: Two kids both want to go first. What is a quick, fair way to decide?
cards.note: Rock, paper, scissors gives both kids the same chance.

cards.q: Two friends have a problem. Who gets to tell their side of the story?
cards.note: Listen to both sides before deciding what is fair.

cards.q: How do you show a friend that you are listening?
cards.note: Eyes on the speaker and a quiet mouth show you care.

cards.q: You feel really mad at a friend. What should you do first?
cards.note: A deep breath helps your brain calm down so you can talk.

cards.q: Your friend took your pencil. What is a good thing to say?
cards.note: Say what you want in a calm, kind voice.

cards.q: Sam wants tag. Jo wants ball. They play tag first, then ball. What is that called?
cards.note: Each friend gives a little, and both get to play.

cards.q: Ella knocked down Ben's tower by accident. After she says sorry, what can she do?
cards.note: Saying sorry and helping fix it makes things right.

cards.q: A friend says sorry and really means it. What kind thing can you say back?
cards.note: Forgiving a friend helps you both feel better.

cards.q: A kid keeps pushing in line. You asked them to stop. What do you do next?
cards.note: If asking does not work, a grown-up can help.

cards.q: The whole class sits in a circle to talk about a problem. What is that called?
cards.note: In a class meeting, everyone gets a chance to talk.

cards.q: The teacher asks who wants to be line leader. How do kids show they want it?
cards.note: Raising a hand is a calm way to say 'pick me'.

cards.q: The class votes on a story. Eight kids pick the bear book. Five pick the fish book. Which wins?
cards.note: The choice with the most votes wins. Eight is more than five.

cards.q: In a class vote, how many votes does each kid get?
cards.note: One kid, one vote. That keeps it fair.
